verdict: depot.render.js is a genuinely strong artifact on almost every axis the rubric measures: it is a pure string builder with zero DOM/async/global access, it survives every malformed view I threw at it (12 shapes, incl. undefined/null/primitives — 0 throws), it escapes player text and whitelists rarity colours to a hex literal, it declares routes.js/depot.js/index.js as authorities instead of copying their numbers, and it labels two dead hooks (view.lot, carrier.blocked) honestly with what to grep. Five of its cross-file claims were checked against the real files and all five held. It is undone by one primitive. `const N = (v) => { const n = Number(v); return Number.isFinite(n) ? n : null; }` maps null to 0, because Number(null) === 0. The file's own comment three lines above asserts the opposite, and three more comments downstream assert it again. index.js sends null for exactly these columns, so on the default first-run board the ratified Meridian Haulage price-ceiling row renders as `0` Cinder/unit-hop (the cheapest offer on the board) and `0 · full` in red, and any player carrier with an unpublished tariff or an unreturned free_bays column does the same plus a false 'Every bay this carrier has is loaded' banner. That inverts the ratified anti-lockout decision in the one place the player reads it, and it is the exact hunt-list failure: a comment asserting a rule the code does not enforce.
biggest_gap: N() treats null as 0 (Number(null) === 0), so every 'unknown is not zero' guarantee in the file is false for the null values index.js actually sends. Fix N to return null for null/'' before the Number() coercion, then re-check the six call sites that pass an already-N'd value into fmt(x, '—') — fmt re-runs N on it, which is the second half of the same bug. Verify with renderTransport({tab:'exchange'}): the synthesised Meridian row must print '—' for tariff and '—' (not '0 · full') for free bays.
evidence:
public/src/transport/depot.render.js:110 `const N = (v) => { const n = Number(v); return Number.isFinite(n) ? n : null; };` — Number(null)===0, so N(null)===0. Contradicted by its own comment at :106-109 ('N answers null for anything non-finite so a missing column can render as — ... or, worse, as 0'), by :688-689 on the synthesised NPC row ('No invented tariff. `null` prints —; a 0 here would read as "free", which is the opposite of what this carrier is'), by :741-743 ('An unpublished tariff prints —, never 0'), and by :747-750 ('FREE BAYS: null is UNKNOWN and prints —'). Also latent in fmt() at :111-115, which calls N() on a value the caller already passed through N(), so fmt(null,'—') returns 0 rather than the dash. Measured, not theorised: node -e renderTransport({tab:'exchange'}) emits `🚚 Meridian Haulage NPC · fallback · price ceiling0100%0 pairs0 · full`. index.js:322-327 sends `freeBays: null` when the column is absent and index.js:338 sends `freeBays: null` for the NPC unconditionally; index.js:334 sends `tariff: cap > 0 ? cap : null`, which is null on a board with no published player rates — i.e. day one. A carrier row with freeBays:null additionally emits the false banner 'Every bay this carrier has is loaded, so they cannot take another haul right now.' Separately, depot.render.js:891 `CONTRACT_STATE[status]` is an unguarded prototype lookup: a contract with status 'constructor' or 'toString' resolves to a truthy Object.prototype member instead of falling to the 'not one this build recognises' branch, and renders `
` — an empty red banner, the exact blank the file exists to prevent.
